meta.note: Every value here is binding. A render that deviates from any of it is a bug, not a variation. Change the version before changing a value, and never change an entry under `invariants` without a measured reason.

changelog.change: Captions and pictures appear on the word that names them, and the OR disc lands on the word 'or'. The question is synthesised in three segments to make those moments exact.
changelog.reason: Owner's direction. It also removes a small dishonesty in the old timing: both options used to be on screen from the block's first frame while the voice was still working up to them, so the viewer could read ahead of the question and the countdown was measuring a decision they had already started making.

changelog.change: Typeface is Roboto Black Italic, embedded as a woff2 from @fontsource. The synthetic skew is removed and the outlines drop from 10-14px to 6-8px.
changelog.reason: The owner identified the reference face. Roboto ships a real Black Italic, so the skew that stood in for it on Nunito would now double the slant. The lighter outline is theirs too, and it is the right call: at 10-14px on a Black weight the stroke stopped reading as an outline and started reading as a second typeface drawn around the first.

changelog.change: The seam pulse moves from the line to a soft gradient glow: 3.4x scale and a white flash become 1.35x and a bloom that fades to nothing at both edges, over 0.28s in and 0.5s out with sine easing.
changelog.reason: The first version strobed. A hard-edged flash on the one line in the frame pulls the eye off the two options at exactly the moment the viewer is supposed to be choosing between them, which is the opposite of what the pulse is for.

changelog.change: Timer 5.0s → 3.5s. The seam pulses once per second of every tick. New end card: the word COMMENT, a spoken line, the tick continuing one second past it, then the chime. A licensed music bed under the whole video from the owner's cue point.
changelog.reason: Owner's direction. The pulse is the one addition that earns its place structurally: it puts the countdown on screen without drawing a counter, which is what 2.0.0 removed the timer ring to avoid.

changelog.change: Timing is derived from the voiceover instead of fixed. The timer is 5.0s and starts when the question stops. Tick and chime are the owner's own files. The reveal is silent. Percentages are authored, and labelled as authored.
changelog.reason: A fixed 8.5s block had the timer running while the question was still being asked, so the viewer was being timed on a choice they had not finished hearing. Deriving the block from the measured question fixes that and costs only that block lengths now vary — 59.05s for episode 1, still inside the 41-60s band.

changelog.change: Voiceover generated and wired in. Kokoro (af_heart, offline), two clips per block.
changelog.reason: The format does not work without it: the screen shows two fragments and never the stem, so the setup line is the only place the dilemma exists as a question. Hosted providers are all blocked here, but Kokoro's weights ship as GitHub release assets, which the proxy allows.

changelog.change: Sound. Tick, reveal chime and transition swoosh synthesised and wired in; the tick is reinstated as audio only.
changelog.reason: 2.0.0 cut the tick together with the on-screen timer. The visual countdown had to go, but the urgency it carried did not: in the ear it fills the 3.65s decide phase, where nothing on screen moves, without competing with reading two options. The voiceover is still absent — HeyGen and every other provider sit behind the same blocked egress as the images — and it remains the one missing piece that makes the format work, since the stem lives only in the voice.

changelog.change: Full identity replacement. Two full-bleed colour fields split at the middle, one image and one caption per field, an OR badge on the seam, and nothing else. Removed: cards, borders, rounded corners, dark background, vignette, timer ring, VS badge, episode badge, progress dots, fill bars. Copy model changed from whole sentences to a shared spoken stem plus two short fragments.
changelog.reason: 1.x was designed from reasoning about the mechanic rather than from what the winning videos in this niche actually look like, and it showed: chrome the format does not use, and options twice as long as the ones that work. The reference the user supplied shows the real shape — flat red over flat blue, one cut-out subject per side, heavy outlined lowercase captions, an OR disc on the seam. Its captions read 'pain again' and 'sadness again': 10 and 13 characters, sharing an unstated stem. The mined comment vocabulary corroborates it — pain (79), sadness (31), cold (36), single (33), glow (45) are those fragments, and that evidence was already in hand and read only as copy input.

changelog.change: Fonts, winner surface alpha, option length — all corrected against a real renderer. Superseded by 2.0.0.
Rewrote the invariants list to match the spec it sits in, and re-framed the image source as an explicitly unresolved fallback rather than a settled choice.
changelog.reason: The invariants had drifted three versions behind the sections above them: they still named Nunito 900 skewed -8deg and fixed 8500ms blocks, both of which 3.1.x and 3.2.0 replaced. An invariant that contradicts the spec is worse than a missing one — it is the shortest file in the repo and the first thing read, so a contradiction there propagates straight into the composition. Separately, images.source.why argued from one session's egress policy, which reads as a design rationale once that session is gone; the constraint and the decision are now stated apart, and the decision is marked open.

canvas.note: There is no background colour. The two fields cover the frame edge to edge, split at the exact middle.

safe_areas.note: The Shorts player draws its own UI over the frame. Captions and percentages must stay clear of these bands. An image may bleed into the bottom band — it is composed so its subject sits in its upper half — because the caption, not the picture, carries the meaning.

timeline.block_length: variable — derived from the question, not fixed
timeline.formula_s: lead_in 0.2 + stem + gap 0.15 + option A + gap 0.15 + 'or' + option B + timer 3.5 + hold 2.5 + exit 0.35
timeline.computed_by: scripts/build_episode.py, from vo.setup_duration measured by make_voiceover.py
timeline.why_variable: The timer starts when the question stops speaking, never before. A fixed block would either cut a long question short or leave a short one sitting in silence, and the viewer would be deciding while still being told what the choice is.

phases.name: question
phases.note: the voice asks and the screen fills as it goes: option A on its word, then the OR disc, then option B. Nothing is on screen that has not been said.

phases.name: timer
phases.note: 3.5s of the supplied tick. Audible, plus one pulse of the seam per second — the countdown is felt, never drawn as a counter.

phases.name: reveal
phases.note: percentages slam in with the chime, the losing field darkens. No voiceover.

phases.name: hold
phases.note: 2.5s, silent, long enough for the chime to ring out

timeline.band_note: 41-60s is the only duration band that performs in this niche (median 26,239 views against 751 for 16-25s and 8,834 above 60s). Both make_voiceover.py and build_episode.py warn when an episode falls outside it — with five blocks the questions have roughly 3.4s each of headroom before it does.

end_card.structure: one word on screen, the closing line spoken, the tick running underneath, one second of tick alone after the line, then the chime rings the video out
end_card.or_disc: stops with the last block. The end card is one word, alone.

reveal_on_word.rule: Each caption and its picture appear on the word that names them; the OR disc lands on the word 'or'.
reveal_on_word.how: The question is synthesised in three segments — stem, option A, 'or' + option B — so the moment each fragment is named is exact by construction rather than estimated.
reveal_on_word.why_not_alignment: Forced alignment was the alternative. Whisper's model download is blocked by the same egress policy as everything else here, but this is the better answer regardless: a construction that cannot drift beats a measurement that can, and the beat before each option is how these lines are read aloud anyway.
reveal_on_word.cost: The frame is empty for the length of the stem — about 1.9s on the opening block. That is the one real risk in this design: a Shorts viewer decides inside the first second, and an empty split screen is a weaker hook than a dilemma already on screen. Shorten block 1's stem before shortening anything else.

percent.note: The percentage lands on the image, which dims under it.

layout.mirror_note: The two captions sit closest to the seam and the two images push outward. The viewer compares the words, so the words are what the eye finds first.

pulse.at: every second of every tick, including the end card
pulse.carried_by: a vertical gradient glow, not the line
pulse.note: A gradient fading to nothing at both edges has no edge to catch the eye, so the beat registers as light rather than as movement. The line itself barely thickens — 3.4x with a white flash, as in 3.1.0, read as a strobe rather than a breath. Asymmetric in/out and sine easing at both ends leave no corner in the motion, and 0.78s total sits well inside the one-second gap so two pulses never overlap.
pulse.implementation: A pair of tweens, never a repeating one: a repeat does not survive seeking, and the renderer seeks every frame.

color.note: Two colours, full strength, edge to edge, plus black for the outline and the badge. White on #FF1E1E is 3.85:1 and on #0A84FF is 3.65:1, both clearing AA for large text before the outline is even counted. The outline is what makes the caption survive whatever photograph sits behind it.

typography.font_note: Embedded from the file rather than named. Roboto is one of the renderer's bundled families, but a bundle carries the cuts it carries — asking for one it does not ship yields a synthetic approximation, not the real thing, and Black Italic is exactly the kind of cut that gets approximated. The woff2 comes from npm (@fontsource/roboto), which the egress policy allows, and sits in the project so nothing is fetched at render time.
typography.slant_note: The slant is the typeface's own italic, not a skew. 3.1.x faked it with skewX(-8deg) on Nunito; with a real italic cut that transform would double the angle, so it is gone. This is also why the font cannot be swapped for an upright family without revisiting the look.
typography.stroke_note: Thin relative to the letterform: the outline is there to keep the type readable over whatever sits behind it, not to be part of the lettering. 3.1.x ran 10-14px, which on Roboto Black read as a second typeface drawn around the first.

motion.note: Four moves in the whole video: things arrive, the number slams, the loser darkens, things leave. Version 1.x had a depleting timer ring, a VS disc, progress dots and animated fill bars; none of them appear in the videos that win, and each one was another thing competing with a decision the viewer makes in three seconds.

voiceover.tone: fast, dry, mildly provocative; never explains the joke
voiceover.stem_note: Line 1 speaks the stem and both fragments — 'would you rather never feel pain again, or sadness again'. The screen only ever shows the fragments, so the voiceover is what makes the dilemma a sentence. This is why voiceover is required rather than a nice-to-have: without it the two captions are not a question.

engine.name: Kokoro
engine.why: Every hosted TTS is unreachable from these sessions — HeyGen, Microsoft's Edge voices, Google Translate and ElevenLabs all answer 403 through the egress proxy. GitHub release assets do get through, which is where Kokoro publishes its weights, so this is the one free route that works here. Generation itself touches no network.

voiceover.voice_is_identity: The voice is as binding as the palette. A channel is recognised by its sound before its layout, so af_heart does not change between episodes without the same argument any invariant would need.
voiceover.silence_note: Nothing is spoken over the reveal. The percentages land with the chime and are not explained, defended, or joked about — a line there would tell the viewer what to think about a number they are still reading.
voiceover.timing_check: make_voiceover.py measures each question and writes its length back into the episode file; build_episode.py derives every block's timing from it. Nothing about the schedule is guessed.

music.gain_note: A bed, not a layer. The questions have to stay in front of it.
music.rights_note: A commercial recording. On YouTube this will almost certainly draw a Content ID claim: the video stays up but monetisation goes to the rights holder, and in some territories it can be blocked. The channel owner's decision, recorded here so it is never a surprise. The source file is gitignored — its licence is theirs to manage, not this repository's to redistribute.

sfx.source: supplied by the channel owner, converted to 48kHz mono WAV

tick.trim: The source runs 40.8s. Kept from its start and cut at 5.0s with a 100ms fade, so the tick pattern always begins where the owner's file begins.

reveal.trim: none — it fits the 2.5s hold plus the exit

sfx.placement_note: Audio is authored at the composition root with absolute times. A plain timed wrapper does not rebase media, so a scene-local data-start inside a block would still be read as root time and only look like it meant something else.

tick_end.at: the start of the end card
tick_end.trim: cut from the source's start, like the block tick, so the pattern always begins where the owner's file begins

audio.placement_note: Audio is authored at the composition root with absolute times. A plain timed wrapper does not rebase media, so a scene-local data-start inside a block would still be read as root time and only look like it meant something else.

copy_rules.model_note: The dilemma is one sentence split three ways. The stem is spoken and never rendered; the two fragments are all the screen shows. 'Would you rather never feel PAIN AGAIN or SADNESS AGAIN' puts ten characters on one card and thirteen on the other, and that is why it reads in the half-second a viewer gives it.
copy_rules.option_length_note: 22 is the hard cap: two lines of Nunito 900 at 96px across the 900px caption box. 16 or under lands on one line and is what the reference videos actually do — treat one line as the target and two as the exception.
copy_rules.shared_tail_note: The two fragments usually end on the same word ('pain again' / 'sadness again'). The repetition is what makes the pair scan as a single choice.
copy_rules.ramp_note: Block 1 is the hook and must land in under two seconds of reading. Block 5 is the one people argue about in the comments.

images.treatment: single subject on the flat colour field, no photographic background, no drop shadow
images.render_note: Fixed 420px with object-fit: contain. A max-width/max-height rule constrains without ever scaling up, and the source files carry small intrinsic dimensions.
images.subject_placement: upper half of the box, so the bottom field's image survives the Shorts UI band

source.why: Chosen under a hard constraint rather than on merit: the session that built this pipeline ran behind an egress policy that returned 403 for every image CDN and every image API, while leaving the npm registry reachable. Artwork therefore had to come from a package. Within that constraint Apache-2.0 beat OpenMoji (CC-BY-SA, share-alike) and Twemoji (CC-BY, attribution), neither of which sits comfortably on a monetised channel.
source.status: fallback — not the intended destination; see images.open_decision
source.known_limit: Emoji are strong for concrete nouns — pizza, a lemon, a battery — and weak for people, feelings and actions, which render as a yellow face. 'Sadness' becomes a circle. Roughly a third of the bank's fragments are in that weak class, and the channel owner rejected the result on sight.

images.upgrade_path: Photographic cut-outs are the stronger treatment and what the reference videos use. They need either an egress policy that allows an image source, or files supplied directly. Swapping them in is a change to image_a/image_b in the bank — nothing in the composition changes.
images.note: The image is what stops the scroll; the caption is what makes it a choice. A block with no image still renders — the field is simply flat, and the composition draws a dashed slot — but that is a missing asset, not a style.

open_decision.question: Where do the images for people, feelings and actions come from?
open_decision.blocked_by: resolved — the constraint was the sandbox, and it is gone off it

options.option: Generated (Gemini image API, or any image model)
options.for: Exact subject on demand — 'a man crying', 'a superhero flying'. One frozen style prompt gives all 96 fragments a single look, which is what makes a channel recognisable. No third-party rights.
options.against: Costs per image (order of a few cents) and needs billing enabled. Style drift between runs unless the prompt is pinned in this file.

options.for: Photographic cut-outs are what the reference videos use, and the strongest treatment of the three. Free, commercially licensed.
options.against: No guarantee the exact subject exists; cut-out step needed (hyperframes remove-background) to meet the no-background rule.

options.option: Keep Noto for concrete nouns, add a second source for people
options.for: Emoji genuinely win on objects; only the weak class needs replacing.
options.against: Two visual languages in one frame unless the second source is chosen to sit beside flat emoji. Tried with unDraw and rejected: its illustrations carry their own background scenery.

open_decision.recommendation: Generate. It is the only option that answers 'a man crying' with a man crying, and the only one where a pinned style prompt makes the whole bank consistent. Freeze the winning prompt into this section as images.style_prompt so the look is reproducible, exactly as the voice is pinned to am_adam.
open_decision.on_adopting: Change image_a/image_b in content/dilemmas.json to point at the new files and re-run the export step. Nothing in the composition changes — the box is 420px with object-fit: contain and does not care what it is given.

reveal_mechanic.fabrication_note: Changed in 3.0.0 at the channel owner's decision, against the evidence and with it recorded. The most-liked comment across every breakout video mined is people mocking percentages — 'How tf is 90 % and 15%', 148 likes — and the failure they catch is arithmetic, not provenance: numbers that do not add to 100. So the rule that survives is the one that matters in practice, and validate_content.py enforces it. A block that carries invented numbers says so in its own source field: 'authored' never masquerades as a counted result.
reveal_mechanic.split_note: Under 55/45 reads as a coin flip and provokes nothing. Over 88/12 reads as a non-dilemma. Authored splits are held to the same 55-88 band, and an episode should carry at least one deliberately lopsided result — the viewer discovering they are in a minority is the whole engine.

end_card.cta_rule: One line, one ask, pointing at the poll. Never 'like and subscribe'.
end_card.treatment: The two fields stay. The end card is copy on the same split, not a new screen.
end_card.loop_note: Last frame carries the same two fields as the first, so the Shorts loop is seamless.

invariants: Exactly 5 dilemma blocks, then the end card
Block length is variable, derived from the spoken question (timeline.formula_s) — never a fixed duration
Two full-bleed colour fields split at y=960 — no background, no cards, no borders, no corners
Field A is always on top and always #FF1E1E; field B is always below and always #0A84FF
A black OR disc sits on the seam for the dilemma blocks, and is gone for the end card
Roboto Black Italic, white with a thin black outline — the slant is the typeface's own italic, never a skew transform
One image per option: single subject, no photographic background, no drop shadow
No on-screen timer, no progress dots, no episode badge, no fill bars
Nothing appears on screen before the voice has said it
The reveal is silent — the percentages land with the chime and nothing explains them
Percentages always sum to 100, sit in the 55–88 band, and declare their source
No intro: frame 1 is already a dilemma
No borrowed IP, characters, or footage
